rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template for the child's revised section 2. Both provisions cover personnel serving under war-service indefinite appointments who leave a federal position for external service, are reached in regular order for probational appointment from an appropriate civil-service register, or could have received competitive status under Civil Service Rule III with agency-head approval, and then are deemed to have acquired competitive status as of the relevant appointment or classification date. This is unusually specific, substantially parallel legal machinery and language. C04 is also materially used in the child's added deeming provision concerning active-duty status and continuous federal service as of September 30, 1949, but it is secondary to C01. C06 shares the underlying international-organization transfer and reemployment framework, though its individualized five-year exception is less directly reflected in the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any employee serving under a war-service indefinite appointment who is transferred to a public international organization ... and ... is either reached in regular order for probational appointment from a civil-service register appropriate for filling the position in which he was serving or could, with the approval of the head of such agency, have been given a competitive status under Civil Service Rule III if he had remained in the position in which he last served in a Federal agency, shall be considered as having acquired a competitive status as of the date he is reached for probational appointment or classification.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any officer or employee ... serving under a war service indefinite or temporary indefinite appointment and who is reached in regular order for probational appointment from a Civil Service register appropriate for filing the position in which he was serving ... or who could, with the approval of the head of the agency in which he was serving, have been given a competitive status under Civil Service Rule III if he had remained in his former position, shall be considered as having a competitive status as of the date he is reached for probational appointment or classification.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reproduces C01's distinctive eligibility alternatives, agency-approval condition, Civil Service Rule III counterfactual, and deemed acquisition date, adapting the external assignment from the Foreign Service to a public international organization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall be considered ... as having been in an active-duty status on September 30, 1949 ... and as having had continuous service with the Federal Government
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The incumbent in an active duty status ... on the date of this order ... has had continuous service with the Federal Government
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly adapts C04's September 30, 1949 active-duty and continuous-service predicates so transferred employees can qualify under that directive.

shared_material.child_excerpt: for a period not to exceed three years from the date of transfer ... be considered as being on leave of absence ... Provided, that the employee is subsequently reemployed by the Federal Government
shared_material.parent_excerpt: service in the public international organization to which the employee is transferred shall be terminated within three years from the date of such transfer to entitle the employee to the reemployment rights
shared_material.explanation: C06 reflects the same underlying three-year international-organization transfer and federal reemployment machinery, but its specific purpose was an individualized extension to five years, making it a weaker template than C01 or C04.
